Dear all,=0AI am trying to use the survey design engine to place a set of =
=0Asystematic transects in my study area. I had some trouble to import the =
X Y coordinates, I just copied and paste as I am supposed to, but in some w=
ay it seems to be using just two digits of each coordinate. =0AI mean, my c=

hen the map is plotted is 45 and 53, so when I ask it to make the grid with=

urvey design for flying birds=0A=0ALinda:=0A=0AI can appreciate that you'd =
like your boat to travel in a zigzag for efficiency, and that you want to d=
o snapshots at regular intervals. However, if you place your snapshots at =
fixed distances along the transects, they probably won't end up being syste=
matic with respect to each other (because of the zigzag). Is it impractica=
l to use the Distance survey design engine (systematic grid sampling) to pl=
ace a set of systematic points into your study area, then after that design=
is created, connect up the pattern of points in the most efficient manner?=
=0A=0AYour second matter about differing amounts of effort at distances off=
shore could most simply be addressed by the stratification mechanism you de=
scribe. I believe the Mexico sample project that comes with Distance is an=
example of placing differing amounts of sampling intensity within differen=
t strata.=0A=0AThat's my view, but other design mavens may have more clever=
ideas.=0A=0ALinda Wilson wrote:=0A> Hello=0A> =0A> =0A> I am designing a =
boat survey to estimate tern densities. Our survey area=0A> will approximat=
ely be a coastal strip c. 40km long out to 20km offshore,=0A> which encompa=
sses the breeding colony. As all birds will be flying, we=0A> are using a s=
napshot count method (essentially point counts) with=0A> distance bands wit=
hin a 180 degree arc ahead of the boat, out to 300m.=0A> =0A> =0A> I would=
like some advice on the best way to get a systematic random=0A> design for=
the point counts for such a boat survey. I was planning to=0A> use the Di=
stance programme to design zig-zag line transects within our=0A> survey are=
a. I was then going to have the point count positions located=0A> at e.g. 1=
km intervals along the transect. The idea is that the boat will=0A> travel =
at speed between count points, but slow down to allow the count=0A> to be m=
ade instantaneously.=0A> =0A> =0A> First question is how do I ensure that =
the point counts are allocated=0A> randomly (but systematic)? Could I rando=
mly assign the first count point=0A> within the first 1km of the transect, =
and then space them at equal=0A> distance from that one?=0A> =0A> =0A> Sec=
ondly, there will be areas of lower density further offshore, so I=0A> wou=
ld like to have less effort (fewer point counts) in this area (to=0A> reduc=
e survey time). Can I simply space the point counts e.g. every 2km=0A> inst=
ead of 1km in this area, if so how do I then deal with this reduced=0A> eff=
ort during analysis stages? Or do I first need to split the survey=0A> are=
a into two strata, design the zig-zag transects, and then position=0A> the =
point counts. =0A> =0A> Or should I be doing something completely differen=
t?!=0A> =0A> =0A> Thanks=0A> =0A> Linda=0A> =0A> =0A> =0A> Linda J Wilso=

messages.subject: Re: Boat survey design
parts:
Hi Cristine, (cc list)

I just tried it in Distance 6.0 release 2 and it worked fine for me.

Check under File | Project Properties | Geographic that the Geographic=20
coordinate system is none and the shapefile units are meters. You might=20
get the behaviour you describe if Distance thinks you're entering lat=20
and long coordinates.

Another potential problem might arise if you use a comma "," instead of=20
period "." to denote the decimal in your region. If your Windows=20
settings are such that it's expecting a "," then you'd need to enter
452564,0347 5334957,719

If neither of these work, send me a copy of your project (use File |=20
Export project... and save as type zip) and I'll see if I can see what=20
the problem is by looking at it.

Cheers - Len
